I was pretty well addicted And we would play with my friends and I would draw things about sack boy and all sorts of things And I remember one of the things that I built cuz I saw someone use it in a level was a time reversal bot Which is a robot that can rewind time if you press a button, it functions just like the in-game rewind button in create mode, except you can use it during play mode and you can determine what gets rewound. turns.response_html:
LittleBigPlanet 2 logic was an absolute golden era for creative engineering. LBP2's introduction of microchips, sequencers, combiners, and memorizers basically turned a fun platformer into a visual programming playground.

Recreating a time-reversal mechanic in Play Mode was legendary—and you’re completely right, it was surprisingly complex depending on how authentic you wanted the rewind to feel.

How standard "Time Rewind" bots were built in LBP2

Because LBP didn't have a native "global rewind" logic wire for Play Mode, creators had to engineer clever workarounds:

  • The Sequencer Recording Loop:
    • Forward Tracking: A Sequencer set to continuous loop would act as a rolling buffer for input or movement states.
    • The Trigger Switch: Hitting the rewind button triggered a Selector that flipped the Sequencer into Reverse Playback Mode (or reversed its speed), feeding recorded movement or force vectors backward into Movers or Rotators.
  • Breadcrumb / Emitter Tracking:
    • For free-roaming bots, creators often used a trail of invisible, non-colliding "tracking nodes" (emitted every fraction of a second with short lifetimes).
    • When rewind was activated, the bot would turn off its normal AI, turn on an Attract-O-Gel or Follower gadget targeted at those trailing nodes, and pull itself backward along its exact prior path while step-counting backward through a Counter.
  • State Memorization (The "Snapshot" method):
    • For selective rewinding (e.g., restoring broken objects or health), Memorizer chips and Counters captured binary states (doors opened/closed, switch states, health pools). Reversing sent a pulse that reset the registers in reverse order.
  • Visual & Audio Polish:
    • To complete the illusion, creators hooked the rewind trigger into a Global Audio/Visual Tweaker—adding a grainy VHS filter, desaturating the color palette, and playing a reverse tape-rewind sound effect.

The LBP Nazi Zombies Phenomenon

Your recreate-to-play instinct was shared by an entire generation of LBP players. The LBP community’s obsession with rebuilding Call of Duty: Nazi Zombies was unmatched.

Building a functional Zombies map in LBP was a badge of honor because it required chaining almost every core system together:

  • Points Economy: Counters wired to score targets to track money earned per hit/kill.
  • Buyable Debris & Walls: Emitters connected to Score Sensors that subtracted points before destroying wall barriers.
  • Mystery Box: A randomized Selector connected to an Emitter that spawned a random weapon (or a trick item).
  • Wave Controllers: Sequencers that monitored remaining enemy counts, scaled zombie health, and triggered the round-start horn.

It's wild to look back on how much raw logic and systemic thinking people picked up just by messing around with microchips in LBP2's Create Mode.
